cards.explanation: The answer is to agree with each other in the Lord. Paul writes, "I urge Euodia and Syntyche to agree with each other in the Lord." (Philippians 4:2) Euodia and Syntyche are two women Paul names in his letter. Notice he says "…in the Lord," so the agreeing happens with Him in the middle. I think that's a good recipe for any disagreement, friends.

The answer is True. Paul says, "…I ask you, my true yokefellow, to help these women who have contended at my side for the gospel…" (Philippians 4:3) The writer doesn't name this yokefellow, so we leave the name blank too. A yokefellow is someone yoked alongside you, pulling the same load. Euodia and Syntyche get named, and this helper gets the job.

The answer is that they worked at his side to spread the gospel. Paul calls them women "…who have contended at my side for the gospel…" (Philippians 4:3) They didn't watch from the sidelines. They were in it right next to Paul. That's a compliment worth framing, friends, and I'd frame it next to my best batch.
The answer is False. Paul writes, "Rejoice in the Lord always." (Philippians 4:4) He doesn't add any conditions, and he says it twice. Always means always, friends, even on a burnt-batch kind of day.

The answer is gentleness. Paul writes, "Let your gentleness be apparent to all." (Philippians 4:5) Apparent means other people can see it. Gentleness isn't something to stash in the back of the pantry, bakers. Put it out front where everyone can see it.

The answer is False. Paul says, "Be anxious for nothing, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God." (Philippians 4:6) No exceptions made for the big stuff or the small stuff. Everything goes to God in prayer, friends.

The answer is to present them to God with thanksgiving. Paul says, "…in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God." (Philippians 4:6) Notice the thanksgiving rides along with the asking, bakers. Every request goes straight to God Himself.

The answer is True. Paul says, "…the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus." (Philippians 4:7) Guard is a strong word, friends. I think of a doorkeeper standing watch over the whole place, and it all happens in Christ Jesus.

The answer is think. Paul says, "…think on these things." (Philippians 4:8) After the whole list of true, honorable, right, pure, lovely and admirable, the instruction is to think. Fill the mind with the good stuff, bakers, like filling a cookie box with the good batch.

The answer is to put it into practice. Paul says, "Whatever you have learned or received or heard from me, or seen in me, put it into practice." (Philippians 4:9) Learning is only half the batch, friends. The other half is doing it. Then comes the promise: "…the God of peace will be with you."
